title: Information Gathering
summary: Learn everything about the target before touching it hard: live hosts, open ports, running services and versions, and how the web app works. Most of a box is won here.

sections.title: Host Discovery & Port Scanning
steps: Confirm the host is up (ping / nmap -sn)
Fast full TCP port sweep: nmap -p- --min-rate 10000
Deep scan the open ports: nmap -sV -sC -p<ports>
Scan top UDP ports (SNMP, DNS, TFTP...): nmap -sU --top-ports 100
Note every service + exact version for later CVE lookups

sections.title: Service Enumeration / Footprinting
steps: Enumerate each open service one by one
Check for anonymous / guest / null access
Grab banners, versions, certificates and config leaks
Pull usernames, shares, files and hostnames where possible

sections.title: Web Recon
steps: Fingerprint the tech stack (whatweb, Wappalyzer, response headers)
Directory & file brute force (ffuf, feroxbuster, gobuster)
Virtual host & subdomain discovery (ffuf -H Host, gobuster vhost)
Read source, JS files, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and comments
Find login pages, upload forms and parameters to test later

title: Vulnerability Assessment
summary: Turn the enumeration data into a list of things that might be exploitable: known CVEs, web flaws and plain misconfigurations.

sections.title: Known Vulnerabilities (version → CVE)
steps: Map each service version to public CVEs
searchsploit <product version>
Search Google / Exploit-DB / GitHub for PoCs
Prefer stable, well-understood exploits over noisy ones

sections.title: Web Vulnerabilities
steps: Test inputs for SQL injection
Test for XSS (reflected / stored / DOM)
Test for file inclusion (LFI / RFI) and path traversal
Test file upload restrictions and SSRF
Check authentication & access control (IDOR, broken auth)

sections.title: Misconfigurations & Default Credentials
steps: Try default / weak creds on every login and service
Look for exposed admin panels, debug pages and backups
Check for open shares, open relays and world-readable files

title: Exploitation
summary: Get your first foothold. Prepare the exploit, test it safely, and land a shell as some user on the target.

sections.title: Service / Network Exploitation
steps: Run the chosen exploit against the service
Understand what the PoC does before firing it
Catch the shell (nc / rlwrap) and stabilise it

sections.title: Web Exploitation
steps: Turn a web flaw into code execution (webshell, SSTI, deserialization)
Abuse file upload or LFI-to-RCE chains
Use found credentials / tokens to reach admin features

sections.title: Password Attacks
steps: Online brute force / spraying (hydra, crackmapexec)
Crack captured hashes (hashcat, john)
Reuse found passwords across services

title: Post-Exploitation
summary: You have a shell. Enumerate from the inside, hunt for secrets, and escalate to root / SYSTEM.

sections.title: Local Enumeration
steps: Who am I, my groups and my privileges
Run LinPEAS / WinPEAS and read the output
Check sudo -l, cron jobs, services, SUID/SGID and capabilities
List processes, open ports and installed software

sections.title: Privilege Escalation (Linux / Windows)
steps: Exploit misconfigs: sudo rules, SUID binaries, capabilities, writable paths
Windows: token privileges, unquoted service paths, AlwaysInstallElevated
Kernel exploits as a last resort

sections.title: Looting & Credential Hunting
steps: Grab flags and sensitive files
Search configs, history, backups and DBs for passwords
Dump hashes / tokens for reuse (lateral movement)

title: Lateral Movement
summary: If more hosts are in scope, use what you looted to pivot through the internal network and reach new targets.

sections.title: Pivoting & Tunneling
steps: Map the internal network from the foothold
Set up tunnels / proxies (ssh -L/-D, chisel, ligolo)
Reach services only exposed internally

sections.title: Credential Reuse & Pass-the-Hash
steps: Spray looted creds across internal hosts (crackmapexec)
Pass-the-hash / pass-the-ticket where NTLM/Kerberos allows
Repeat the full methodology on each new host

title: Active Directory
summary: A dedicated track for AD environments (big for CPTS & OSCP). Enumerate the domain, abuse misconfigurations, and work toward Domain Admin.

sections.title: AD Enumeration
steps: Enumerate users, groups, computers and shares (enum4linux-ng, ldapsearch, rpcclient)
Map the domain with BloodHound (SharpHound / bloodhound-python)
Find the attack paths to high-value targets

sections.title: AD Attacks
steps: AS-REP roasting (users without pre-auth)
Kerberoasting (crack service account tickets)
Abuse ACLs / delegation / GPO misconfigurations

sections.title: Domain Dominance & Lateral Movement
steps: Move with PtH / PtT via WinRM, WMI, SMBexec, PsExec
DCSync to dump domain hashes
Golden / Silver tickets for persistence
